eCommerce Data Scraping Services | Product Data Scraping Agency 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 eCommerce Data Scraping Services 
 Access real-time, accurate product data from marketplaces, supplier sites, review platforms, and more to power smarter business decisions.

 Receive scraped data on your chosen daily, weekly, or real-time frequency 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Talk to us 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Streamline Real-Time eCommerce Product Data Scraping for Large-Scale Catalogs 
 Need real-time product data for thousands of SKUs without the delays? While several automated/AI tools and APIs promise seamless automated data extraction, they often struggle or fail to scrape data when: 
 
 
 
 
 Website structure changes 
 
 
 
 
 SKUs increases 
 
 
 
 
 Encounter protected web-sources with strict anti-scraping mechanisms 
 
 
 
 
 We eliminate these challenges with our product data scraping services. The seasoned data scraping team at SAMM data specializes in extracting real-time, accurate eCommerce data (product titles, descriptions, prices, and competitor insights) from any specified web source, including eCommerce marketplaces, supplier feeds, manufacturer websites, and review platforms. 
 
 Leveraging custom scripts, API, and reliable data scraping tools, we extract product information from targeted websites and clean, enrich, and structure it in ready-to-use formats (CSV, JSON, XML). Our continuous monitoring ensures scraped data remains up to date, while stringent QA protocols verify accuracy at scale. Whether you're conducting competitor analysis, optimizing pricing strategies, or analyzing market trends, we provide clean, structured data consistently, reliably, and at scale. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Addressing Complex Product Data Scraping Challenges to Fuel Smarter eCommerce Decisions 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Anti-Scraping Mechanisms & Access Barriers 
 Problem: Modern websites deploy sophisticated bot detection, CAPTCHA, IP blocking, and rate limiting to prevent automated data access. 
 Solution: We utilize proxy networks, implement intelligent request patterns that mimic human behavior, employ CAPTCHA-solving technologies, rotate user agents, and use session management techniques to scrape product data from such websites. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Dynamic & JavaScript-Heavy Content 
 Problem: Many eCommerce platforms use JavaScript frameworks to dynamically load product data, making traditional data scraping methods ineffective. 
 Solution: We employ headless browsers, execute JavaScript rendering, handle AJAX requests, manage asynchronous content loading, and interact with single-page applications to capture data that loads progressively or on demand. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Inconsistent Data Structures Across Platforms 
 Problem: Each marketplace uses different HTML structures, CSS classes, data formats, and naming conventions, making unified data collection extremely complex. 
 Solution: We develop platform-specific extraction logic, create unified data schemas, and map disparate data structures to consistent formats, ensuring standardized output regardless of source complexity. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Website Changes & Maintenance Overhead 
 Problem: eCommerce websites constantly update their layouts, structure, and security measures, disrupting scrapers' functionality and requiring continuous maintenance. 
 Solution: We proactively monitor target websites, implement adaptive scraping logic that automatically handles minor structural changes, maintain version-controlled scraper code, and update extraction logic within hours of detecting website changes. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Data Quality & Accuracy Issues 
 Problem: Scraped data often contains inconsistencies, missing values, formatting errors, duplicates, outdated information, and contextual inaccuracies, making market research & analysis challenging. 
 Solution: Using a human-in-the-loop approach, we validate every dataset against multiple sources,

Investment screening Identify undervalued properties by tracking price/sqft trends, days-on-market signals, price-cut history, and rental-yield gaps across target markets. Agent lead generation Daily feeds of new listings, price changes, and expired listings in target geographies — sized for territory-level outreach by agents and brokerages. Proptech product feeds Power your home-valuation tool, rental-comp engine, mortgage product, or buyer-search interface with normalized public listing data refreshed on a schedule. Commercial real estate signals Track office listings, retail vacancies, industrial space, and asking rents across CoStar-adjacent public sources and regional commercial portals. Short-term rental intelligence Airbnb and VRBO public listing data — occupancy, nightly rate, length-of-stay patterns, and supply density by neighborhood for investors and operators. Portals we scrape Major US, UK, EU, and APAC real estate portals. Regional and niche portals scoped per engagement — including commercial, agricultural, and short-term rental sources. Zillow Redfin Realtor.com Trulia Homes.com Rightmove (UK) Zoopla (UK) idealista (ES) Immobilienscout24 (DE) SeLoger (FR) Domain.com.au REA.com.au Airbnb (public) Apartments.com Fields we extract Every attribute a valuation, agent, or investor model needs. Full address & geo (lat/lon) ZIP, neighborhood, MSA, county List price & price history Beds, baths, square footage Lot size & year built Days on market Status (active, pending, sold) Sold price & sold date Listing agent & brokerage Property type & subtype Photos & virtual tour links School district & ratings HOA fees & property taxes Rental rate & rent history Why this is hard Real estate portals are fragmented, geo-messy, and frequently re-listed. The same physical property can appear on Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com, and the local brokerage site — with different prices, different photos, and different "days on market" because each portal counts time-on-market its own way. Without cross-portal deduplication, an inventory report becomes triple-counted noise. Address parsing is the next problem. "123 Main St #4B" on one portal becomes "123 Main Street, Unit 4B" on another and "123 Main St Apt 4B" on a third. We resolve all variants to a canonical address with lat/lon, ZIP, neighborhood, county, and MSA so listings can be joined to your internal datasets and external tax records. Finally: listings disappear. A delisting can mean sold, withdrawn, expired, or re-listed at a new price under a new MLS number. We track listing-history continuity so the same property\'s journey is preserved in your data, not lost when it re-enters the market. The stack underneath is the same as everywhere else: extraction infrastructure , AI normalization , and delivery surfaces . The schemas and matching logic are real-estate-specific. We organize the collected content around your required format, coverage, and delivery needs.  Discuss Your Data Requirements Successful Case Studies 500+ Datasets Delivered 99% Validation Accuracy 24/7 Data Collection 3X Faster Delivery Key Takeaways Purpose-Built Datasets - Collect data around a defined AI, analytics, or research objective instead of relying on broad datasets with limited relevance. Multiformat Collection - Gather text, images, videos, audio, API responses, and supporting metadata through methods suited to each source.  Structured Data Delivery - Organize collected content so it can move into AI workflows, analytics platforms, cloud storage, or connected applications. Common Barriers for Data Collection A useful dataset requires suitable sources, reliable collection methods, and consistent organization. Our team addresses these requirements before the data reaches AI models or downstream systems. Limited Dataset Availability Available datasets may not contain the subject coverage or content required for a particular use case. Our consultants define the required data before reviewing possible sources. This keeps the collection effort aligned with the intended outcome. Data Spread Across Sources  Relevant information may be distributed across websites, APIs, media libraries, and other digital platforms. Our developers build source-specific workflows that bring the required records into one organized dataset. Multiple Content Formats A project may require text, images, videos, audio, and structured records from the same source. We collect each format through a suitable method and preserve the relationships between related files and metadata.  Inconsistent Source Structures Different websites and platforms often use different page layouts, file names, and metadata fields. Our team maps collected content into a consistent schema. This makes the resulting dataset easier to use and maintain.  Duplicate or Missing Records Automated collection can result in duplicate files and overlooked content when pages and source structures change. Our developers use validation checks to identify duplicate records and incomplete collection runs. They retry failed items or flag them for review.  Outdated Source Content Datasets lose value when source information changes, and the collection process is manual. Our team builds scheduled workflows that capture new or updated content at the required frequency.  Data Collection Services for AI and Analytics We collect and prepare information from approved sources for AI , analytics , and research. Each engagement turns variable source content into a reliable dataset that is ready for downstream use. We configure each workflow around source coverage, content requirements, and update frequency. Delivery capacity is what actually constrains them — and it never arrives in a convenient shape. Three pitches land in the same week, or a client asks for a stack nobody on staff has touched in years. Hiring against a spike is a twelve-month bet on a two-month problem. So the work goes out. That's where the risk moves: the code still ships with your logo on it, the client still calls you when it breaks, and a subcontractor who introduces themselves on a shared channel can undo years of positioning in an afternoon. A white-label partner gets judged on two things — the engineering, and staying invisible while doing it.  When agency teams are at capacity, client expectations do not slow down. FYC Labs provides white-label overflow development support so agencies can deliver complex work on time without stretching internal resources too thin. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Scale Delivery Without Expanding Payroll 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Agencies often face short bursts of heavy development demand when multiple client projects launch at once. Hiring full-time staff for temporary surges is expensive and can create unnecessary overhead once workloads normalize. Overflow development gives agencies a flexible way to increase capacity only when they need it. This helps teams stay responsive without committing to permanent headcount. It also reduces pressure on account managers who need reliable delivery timelines. The result is a more scalable operating model that protects margins. 
 White-label support makes this scaling process even smoother because the additional developers can work under the agency's brand. Clients continue to experience the agency as the primary delivery partner, which preserves trust and continuity. Internal teams can assign tasks more confidently knowing there is backup available for frontend, backend, QA, or full-stack work. This approach is especially useful during seasonal spikes, product launches, and redesigns. Agencies can take on more business without risking burnout. Capacity becomes a strategic advantage instead of a recurring problem. Overflow development also helps agencies stay nimble in competitive markets where speed can determine whether a deal is won or lost. Instead of turning away new work, leaders can expand delivery capability quickly. That flexibility can improve revenue opportunities while keeping project quality high. It also gives sales teams more confidence when promising timelines to prospective clients. Agencies that can scale on demand are better positioned to grow sustainably. In practice, this means fewer missed deadlines and more successful client relationships. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Protect Client Relationships with Reliable Execution 
 
 Client trust is built on consistent communication and dependable delivery. When an agency misses deadlines because the team is overloaded, the damage often extends beyond a single project. Overflow development support helps prevent those bottlenecks by adding experienced engineers when internal bandwidth runs low. That means milestones are met more predictably and clients see steady progress. Agencies can focus on strategy and relationship management while technical execution continues moving forward. Reliability becomes part of the agency's reputation. 
 A strong overflow partner should adapt to the agency's workflow rather than forcing a new process on the team. That includes learning the preferred tools, documentation standards, and review process. With the right setup, outside developers can contribute in a way that feels seamless to internal staff. This reduces friction during handoffs and keeps projects aligned with client expectations. It also helps preserve the agency's voice and standards across every deliverable. The smoother the integration, the easier it is to maintain a polished client experience. Reliable execution also lowers the risk of overpromising and underdelivering, which is a common challenge in service businesses. Agencies can accept more ambitious scopes when they know extra engineering support is available. That makes it easier to recover from unexpected scope changes, bugs, or timeline shifts. Instead of scrambling to catch up, teams can respond with a structured plan. Clients notice when an agency can stay calm under pressure. That confidence often leads to stronger retention and more referrals.

 In brief 
 Workflow automation maps your business processes, identifies high-ROI candidates for automation, and builds them. Done well, it recovers 20-40% of admin time. We score every candidate against time saved, error reduction, and payback period — and only build the ones that justify the fee. 
 
 What workflow automation looks like in practice 
 Common workflows we automate for mid-market UK clients: 
 
 Lead-to-customer — capturing leads, scoring, routing, sequenced follow-up, handover to sales. 
 Quote-to-cash — quote generation, e-signature, invoicing, payment reminders. 
 Onboarding — new client/employee onboarding with task assignment, document collection, and welcome flows. 
 Approval flows — invoice approval, expense approval, holiday requests with multi-stage routing. 
 Reporting — automated weekly dashboards pulling from CRM/finance/ops. 
 

 How we score automation ROI 
 
 Time mapping — how many hours/month does this workflow consume? 
 Loaded cost — at the loaded cost of the people running it, what's the £-value? 
 Build cost — what does it cost to automate (build + tooling + ongoing)? 
 Payback period — when does the £-saved cross the £-spent line? 
 
 We only build automations with a payback period under 12 months, ideally under 6.

 Tool-agnostic — we choose based on your stack, your team's skills, and what's maintainable.

Sydney-based, working across Australia. Book a Discovery Call → Take the free assessment What does a business automation agency do? A business automation agency finds the repeating work inside a company, decides which of it can safely be handled by software, and then builds and deploys that software. The work splits three ways: mapping the processes and costing them in hours, building the automation and connecting it to the systems the business already runs on, and putting governance around anything that runs unattended. The distinction that matters when choosing one is delivery — an agency that stops at a recommendation has done the first third and left you to buy the rest. The honest comparison Agency, independent consultant, or hire in-house? All three work. They fail in different ways, and the right answer depends on how much automation you expect to do after the first one. Three ways to get business automation built, and what each one costs you Automation agency Independent consultant In-house hire Typical cost Fixed fee per build, from $3,500 AUD $120–$250/hr, open-ended $120K–$180K/yr fully loaded Time to first result One to eight weeks Depends on their availability Three months before they know your systems Who owns it after You do, with a written playbook Usually you, sometimes them They do — until they leave Breadth of skills Whole team: process, build, integration, governance Whatever that one person is good at Whatever that one person is good at How it fails Scope creep, or a retainer you cannot leave They get busy with another client Key-person risk, and it takes a year to notice Best when You want two or three automations live this quarter You have one narrow, well-understood problem Automation is a permanent, continuous function Our fixed fees are published rather than quoted on request: $3,500 AUD for a Claude Cowork setup, around $8,000 for a multi-team implementation, and from around $10,000 for a Claude Code rollout. Broader programs are scoped in a two-week Discovery first. Consultant rates and in-house salary ranges are indicative Australian market figures for 2026, not quotes — use them to compare shapes, not to budget. How we actually run an automation engagement Hours first, tools second Find the repeating work We map the processes that repeat and cost them in hours and AUD before proposing anything. Most businesses are surprised by which process is actually the expensive one — it is rarely the one that feels most annoying. The step most proposals skip Check the data can be reached Software can only act on what it can get to. Files in someone’s inbox, figures that live in a spreadsheet on one laptop, and approvals that happen verbally are all blockers that no tool solves. We find these before quoting, not after. Working, not demonstrated Build one thing and put it in production One workflow, end to end, running against real data with real failure handling. A pilot that works on curated inputs proves nothing about the Tuesday when the file arrives malformed. Governance in writing Write down what runs unattended Which steps run on their own, which always ask first, what happens when something fails silently, and who is allowed to change that list. This is the part that decides whether an automation is still running in six months. You own it Hand it over The workflows, the configuration and a written playbook your team can extend. We do not build dependencies on ourselves — a retainer you cannot leave is a business model, not an outcome. When hiring an automation agency is the wrong call Three situations where we will tell you not to buy anything yet. Automating an unstable process locks in the instability. A process nobody owns cannot be changed, whatever the software does. And a workflow whose data lives in someone’s inbox has a filing problem, not an automation proble

bountyhub.title: About Us
bountyhub.text: About Us Explore Bounties Leaderboard Pricing Docs About Us Welcome to BountyHub! At BountyHub, we believe in the power of collaboration and innovation. We are dedicated to connecting project maintainers with talented developers to solve issues, enhance projects, and push the boundaries of what’s possible in the world of open source software. Our Mission Our mission is to create a platform that simplifies the process of issue resolution in open source projects. By offering a system where project maintainers can place bounties on GitHub issues and developers can earn rewards by solving these issues, we aim to: Accelerate Development: Speed up the development process by providing incentives for developers to contribute to open source projects. Foster Innovation: Encourage innovative solutions by connecting diverse talent from around the world. Support the Open Source Community: Empower the open source community by providing financial rewards for valuable contributions. Our Story BountyHub was founded by Omar Soufiane a passionate developer who recognized the challenges faced by open source project maintainers in resolving issues and managing contributions and wanted to create a platform that not only addresses these challenges but also rewards contributors for their hard work and dedication. How It Works Create a Bounty: Project maintainers can log in with their GitHub accounts, import issues, and place bounties on them. Solve and Submit: Developers browse available bounties, work on the issues, and submit pull requests. Review and Reward: Once the pull request is merged, the bounty creator reviews the solution. If accepted, the developer receives the bounty reward. Why Choose BountyHub? Seamless Integration: Easily integrate with GitHub to manage issues and contributions. Fair Compensation: Ensure that developers are fairly compensated for their efforts. Community Focused: We are committed to supporting and growing the open source community. Contact Us We love to hear from our users! If you have any questions, feedback, or suggestions, please feel free to reach out to us: Email: [email protected] 131 Continental Dr, Suite 305 Newark, DE 19713 Thank you for being a part of BountyHub. Together, we can make the open source world a better place. taskbounty.text: For OSS Maintainers, Turn Your GitHub Issue Backlog Into Funded Bounties · TaskBounty Skip to content TaskBounty Board Swarms Paid jobs Hire an agent Coverage For developers Free scan Deep Review Secure my app Repo & CI Hardening Autopilot (Beta) Sign in Find your next task For open-source maintainers Fund your GitHub issue backlog. Zero cost to you. TaskBounty is the open-source bounty platform where AI agents and developers compete to fix bugs and ship features on your repo. Maintainers pay nothing. Bounties are funded by sponsors who rely on your project. Every GitHub issue bounty is a chance to hire an AI coding agent or pay a human developer for a pull request, without touching your own budget. Install the GitHub Action Talk to us Why open source maintainers use TaskBounty If you maintain an open-source project, you've probably watched an issue backlog grow faster than you can close it. Enterprise users file bugs, first-time contributors drop half-finished PRs, and the one tricky edge case that blocks a release sits open for three months. TaskBounty exists to unstick that backlog, by turning each issue into a funded bounty that multiple independent solvers can compete on. Unlike single-agent AI tools like Copilot or Cursor, TaskBounty gives you three to five independent solutions for the same issue. You pick the one that fits your codebase and merge it. Because solvers are paid from escrow only when their PR is accepted, the incentive to write code that actually works (and follows your CONTRIBUTING.md) is built in. This is code bounty marketplace economics applied to open source: sponsors fund outcomes, solvers compete on quality, and maintainers get working PRs without writing a single line of code themselves. Who the sponsors are Sponsors include startups that ship on top of your library, enterprises that vendor your code, and individual developers who just want that one bug fixed. TaskBounty aggregates their funding and routes it to the GitHub issues on your repo that match their priorities. You always stay in control of what gets merged. Every fix ships with a regression test Pure win for maintainers: every TaskBounty bug fix includes a regression test that locks the bug in. Our sandbox verifies the test fails on the broken code and passes on the fix, before the PR ever lands in your queue. You merge a fix and a test, not just a patch. How you control quality You keep full review authority. A bounty submission is just a pull request. You approve, request changes, or close it exactly like any other PR. You can disable AI-generated submissions on your repo, or require specific reviewers. Nothing merges without your sign-off. Three ways to get started Install the GitHub Action Label any issue with bounty to open a funded bounty automatically. Three-step install. Setup guide → Add to FUNDING.yml Get a custom sponsor page for your repo. Shows open bounties and lets fans fund new ones with one click. Add funding → Drop a README badge Let users and contributors know they can fund bounties on your repo. One-line Markdown snippet. Generate badge → Show test coverage Add a Codecov-style coverage badge backed by verified Coverage Uplift bounties on your repo. Coverage badge → Frequently asked questions Does this cost my open-source project anything? No. Bounties on your repo are funded by TaskBounty sponsors, companies and individuals who depend on your project and want it to improve. Maintainers never pay. You review PRs like you always do, and solvers get paid out of sponsor-funded escrow. How is this different from GitHub Sponsors? GitHub Sponsors funds you, the maintainer, on a recurring basis. TaskBounty funds specific outcomes, individual GitHub issue bounties tied to concrete PRs. The two are complementary. You can add both to your .github/FUNDING.yml. Do I have to accept AI agent contributions? No. You review and merge PRs exactly as you do today. You can set a repo AI policy that disallows AI-generated submissions, or require human review.  Mautic bounty programme  
 What follows is the Mautic project’s approach to operating a bounty program for contributions to Mautic Core and officially supported Plugins via relevant GitHub repositories. 
 If you have feedback on this policy, please join the next team meeting on Slack in #t-product. Get an invite at Mautic Community Slack . 
 
 About the program  
 The Mautic core team is very small and always looking for new contributors to the Open Source codebase. Mautic’s bounty program is an opportunity to address neglected yet important issues and also allows Mautic members to bring attention to issues they care about by providing a financial incentive. Contributors who fix issues with an associated bounty receive financial compensation through invoices on Open Collective, provided that their contribution meets all requirements and a core team member merges their pull request. 
 
 No compromise on quality  
 Mautic requires all contributions to meet high standards. Pull requests are only accepted if they’re: 
 
 Completed to a high standard 
 Fully covered by automated tests 
 Prepared in a reasonable time frame, including prompt responses to feedback 
 Resolving the linked issue in its entirety 
 For bug fixes, submit the pull request against the upcoming major release branch - for example, 6.x - with a companion PR against the current minor release branch - for example, 5.1. You must meet all quality criteria, and wait for a maintainer to merge the PRs, for payout eligibility. 
 
 Mautic seeks quality contributions only . For general pull request guidelines, see the Mautic-pr-requirements . 
 A contribution is only approved for payment after a maintainers has merged all related pull requests. 
 Developers should only request to work on tasks and projects that they’re confident of completing in their entirety, seen through to completion, and which they’re capable of working on at their current knowledge and skill level. 
 Mautic’s Product Team is happy to answer questions and provide some limited support, but don’t have the capacity to mentor junior developers working on bounty issues - it’s expected developers work on the task without requiring direct support from the team .
